citeAs: Mahmood, N., Ghorbani, N., Troje, N. F., Pons-Moll, G., and Black, M. J. (2019). AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278.
creator: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, Michael J. Black (MPI for Intelligent Systems, Meshcapade GmbH, York University, MPI for Informatics)
description: AMASS is a large and varied database of human motion that unifies 15 different optical marker-based motion capture datasets by representing them within a common framework and parameterization using the SMPL body model. The dataset contains more than 42 hours of motion data, spanning over 346 subjects, more than 11,451 motions, represented as SMPL pose parameters, shape parameters, and soft-tissue (DMPL) coefficients. It is designed to enable machine learning for applications in animation and computer vision.
name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
rai:dataBiases: The paper notes that previous attempts to merge datasets standardize to fixed body proportions, which fundamentally alters the data. AMASS avoids this by working directly with markers and recovering full 3D body surface. The source datasets are each narrowly focused on particular classes of motions, and even the largest ones are limited in size and variety. The SSM dataset used for hyperparameter tuning consists of only three subjects.
rai:dataCollection: 15 existing optical marker-based mocap datasets were collected and unified. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet. Several datasets were obtained privately or recorded by the authors (Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab, and SSM). The SSM dataset was recorded using an OptiTrack motion capture system (24 Prime 17W cameras) with 67 reflective markers per subject, synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanning system (22 stereo camera pairs, 22 color cameras, 34 speckle projectors) capable of 60 fps 3D scans.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Marker occlusion was handled by introducing a variable pose prior weight coefficient q that increases the pose prior weight as a function of the number of missing markers. When hand markers are absent, hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model. Swapped and mislabeled markers were identified through manual inspection and either corrected or excluded.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Optical marker-based motion capture data from 15 different datasets, each using different numbers and placements of reflective markers (ranging from 37 to 91 markers). Source datasets include CMU, MPI-HDM05, MPI-Pose Limits, KIT, BioMotion Lab, TCD, ACCAD, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TotalCapture, and Transitions. The SSM dataset additionally includes synchronized high-resolution 4D body scans.
rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: Source datasets are often narrowly focused on particular classes of motions. The method does not have ground-truth data for evaluating hand articulation accuracy. Current runtime for MoSh++ is not real-time. The method may produce unreliable poses when multiple markers of a particular body part are simultaneously occluded. The SSM dataset used for evaluation consists of only three subjects.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: All source mocap datasets were retargeted to a common SMPL parameterization using MoSh++. Each frame is represented as SMPL 3D shape parameters (16 dimensions), DMPL soft-tissue coefficients (8 dimensions), and full SMPL pose parameters (90 dimensions including hand articulations). The number of shape and dynamics coefficients was optimized using cross-validation on the SSM dataset to avoid overfitting.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: MoSh++ was used to convert raw mocap marker data into SMPL body model parameters (pose, shape, soft-tissue/DMPL coefficients). The method fits the SMPL/DMPL body model to observed mocap markers in two stages: Stage I estimates body shape and latent marker positions from 12 randomly chosen frames; Stage II optimizes pose and soft-tissue deformation for each frame. Results were manually inspected and problems (swapped/mislabeled markers) were either corrected or held out. A variable pose prior weight was applied to handle missing/occluded markers.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors state they will continuously incorporate more mocap data contributed by themselves and the community, and will support the community in adding new captures as long as they can be similarly shared.
rai:dataSocialImpact: AMASS enables new applications that require large amounts of human motion training data, supporting advances in computer vision, animation, and deep learning. The dataset is made publicly available to the research community to democratize access to large-scale human motion data.
rai:dataUseCases: Animation and visualization of human motion; generating training data for deep learning in computer vision; learning models of human motion; generating synthetic training data for computer vision tasks; training models to denoise mocap data; human pose estimation; character motion synthesis and editing.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++ (an extension of MoSh) — an optimization-based method using the SMPL/SMPL-H body model and DMPL soft-tissue model to automatically fit body shape, pose, and soft-tissue parameters to mocap marker data. Uses Powell's gradient-based dogleg minimization implemented in the Chumpy auto-differentiation package.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: Dataset is motion capture data processed by MoSh++; no per-item human annotation count is described.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: No human annotators with demographics described; processing is automated via MoSh++.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: No human annotation process; quality is evaluated via scan-to-mesh distance metrics, not inter-annotator agreement.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No crowdsourcing or annotation platform used; data processing is automated.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: No human annotation protocol; data is processed automatically by MoSh++.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Missing markers are handled by pose prior weighting and default hand poses, not data imputation in the statistical sense.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Paper does not discuss collection of PII or sensitive personal information; subjects are motion capture participants.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific collection timeframe or date range is stated in the paper for the source datasets or the SSM dataset.
